claims.object_text: KNa1.2 (Slick) subunit of the sodium-dependent voltage-gated potassium channel KNa
claims.quote: KCNT1 and KCNT2 respectively encode the KNa1.1 (Slack) and KNa1.2 (Slick) subunits of the sodium-dependent voltage-gated potassium channel KNa.

claims.object_text: epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures (EIMFS)
claims.quote: EIMFS have a genetic origin and are mostly caused by de novo mutations in the KCNT1 gene, and much more rarely in the KCNT2 gene.
Here, we report two novel, de novo truncating mutations of KCNT2: one mutation is frameshift (p.L48Qfs43), is situated in the N-terminal domain, and was found in a patient with EOEE (possibly EIMFS);

claims.object_text: epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures (EIMFS)
claims.quote: the other mutation is nonsense (p.K564*), is located in the C-terminal region, and was found in a typical EIMFS patient.
they decreased the global current density of heteromeric channels by ~25% (p.K564*) and ~55% (p.L48Qfs43).

claims.object_text: reconstituted KNa1.2 homomeric and KNa1.1/KNa1.2 heteromeric channels in transfected chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells
claims.quote: Using whole-cell patch-clamp recordings, we have analyzed the functional consequences of those two novel KCNT2 mutations on reconstituted KNa1.2 homomeric and KNa1.1/KNa1.2 heteromeric channels in transfected chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells.
Overall our data emphasize the involvement of KCNT2 in EOEE
